claim: Visual perception across a broad range of light levels is shaped by interactions between rod- and cone-mediated signals.
source: Visual perception across a broad range of light levels is shaped by interactions between rod- and cone-mediated signals.
evidence: This is a general statement about visual perception presented in the abstract without specific experimental data in this sentence, but is supported by the overall study findings.

claim: Responses of retinal ganglion cells depend on signals from both rod and cone photoreceptors.
source: Because responses of retinal ganglion cells, the output cells of the retina, depend on signals from both rod and cone photoreceptors, interactions occurring in retinal circuits provide an opportunity to link the mechanistic operation of parallel pathways and perception.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Rod- and cone-mediated responses interact nonlinearly to control the responses of primate retinal ganglion cells.
source: Here we show that rod- and cone-mediated responses interact nonlinearly to control the responses of primate retinal ganglion cells
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Rod-cone interactions are asymmetric, with rod responses strongly suppressing subsequent cone responses but not vice-versa.
source: these nonlinear interactions, surprisingly, were asymmetric, with rod responses strongly suppressing subsequent cone responses but not vice-versa.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 1C, D.

claim: Human psychophysical experiments revealed a similar perceptual asymmetry in rod-cone interactions.
source: Human psychophysical experiments revealed a similar perceptual asymmetry.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 1H.

claim: Nonlinear interactions in retinal output cells were well-predicted by linear summation of kinetically-distinct rod- and cone-mediated signals followed by a synaptic nonlinearity.
source: Nonlinear interactions in the retinal output cells were well-predicted by linear summation of kinetically-distinct rod- and cone-mediated signals followed by a synaptic nonlinearity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 4.

claim: Perceptual interactions between rod- and cone-mediated signals have been studied for nearly 200 years.
source: Perceptual interactions between rod- and cone-mediated signals have been studied for nearly 200 years
evidence: This is a historical statement presented without specific citation in this sentence.

claim: Rod-cone interactions influence the spatial, temporal and chromatic sensitivities of human vision at light levels ranging from moonlight to dawn or dusk.
source: these interactions influence the spatial, temporal and chromatic sensitivities of human vision at light levels ranging from moonlight to dawn or dusk (for review see Buck, 2004, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles by Buck.

claim: Little is known about the mechanistic basis of rod-cone interactions.
source: Despite the impact of rod-cone interactions on vision, little is known about the mechanistic basis of such interactions.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field presented as motivation for the study.

claim: ON parasol ganglion cells project to magnocellular layers of the lateral geniculate nucleus.
source: ON parasol ganglion cells (which project to magnocellular layers of the lateral geniculate nucleus)
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge.

claim: ON parasol ganglion cells exhibited particularly robust responses to brief increment flashes.
source: ON parasol ganglion cells (which project to magnocellular layers of the lateral geniculate nucleus) exhibited particularly robust responses to such flashes.
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments described in the Results section.

claim: Ganglion cell spike outputs in response to brief increment flashes were dominated by excitatory synaptic input.
source: ganglion cell spike outputs in response to these flashes were dominated by excitatory synaptic input (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dim short-wavelength flashes preferentially activate rod photoreceptors.
source: We used dim short-wavelength flashes to preferentially activate rod photoreceptors
evidence: This is based on known photoreceptor spectral sensitivities and is supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Brighter long-wavelength flashes preferentially activate L-cone photoreceptors.
source: and brighter long-wavelength flashes to preferentially activate L-cone photoreceptors (Figure 1A,B; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on known photoreceptor spectral sensitivities and is supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The linear sum of ON parasol responses to rod- and cone-preferring flashes delivered individually differed substantially from the response to the flashes delivered together.
source: The linear sum of ON parasol responses to rod- and cone-preferring flashes delivered individually differed substantially from the response to the flashes delivered together (Gouras and Link, 1966) (Figure 1B)
evidence: This is a finding from the current experiments, also supported by a citation to previous work, and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Rod- and cone-mediated signals interact nonlinearly within the retina.
source: that is, rod- and cone-mediated signals interact nonlinearly within the retina.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that linear summation does not match the actual response.

claim: An interaction index of 0 corresponds to linear summation of the responses.
source: an interaction index of 0 corresponds to linear summation of the responses
evidence: This is a definition of the interaction index metric used in the study.

claim: An interaction index of 1 indicates that the adapt flash completely suppressed the response to the test flash.
source: whereas an interaction index of 1 indicates that the 'adapt' flash (i.e., the first flash in the sequence) completely suppressed the response to the 'test' flash (i.e., the second flash in the sequence).
evidence: This is a definition of the interaction index metric used in the study.

claim: Cone responses produced a modest suppression of subsequent rod responses.
source: cone responses produced a modest suppression of subsequent rod responses (cone → rod interaction)
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 1C, D.

claim: Rod responses produced a strong suppression of subsequent cone responses.
source: while rod responses produced a strong suppression of subsequent cone responses (rod → cone interaction; Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 1C, D.

claim: The asymmetry in rod-cone interactions held for rod- and cone-preferring adapt flashes that produced similar amplitude responses in the RGC.
source: This asymmetry held for rod- and cone-preferring adapt flashes that produced similar amplitude responses in the RGC (as in Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, as shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Rod → cone interactions were restricted to a <1 s time window following the adapt flash.
source: Rod → cone interactions were restricted to a <1 s time window following the adapt flash (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 1E, F.

claim: ON midget ganglion cells exhibited qualitatively similar rod-cone interactions to ON parasol cells.
source: ON midget ganglion cells, another prominent retinal ganglion cell type in primate retina, exhibited qualitatively similar rod-cone interactions (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments, though the data is not shown.

claim: Monocular-specific interactions in human perception shared several features with those observed in the responses of ON parasol ganglion cells.
source: Monocular-specific interactions shared several features with those observed in the responses of ON parasol ganglion cells
evidence: This is a comparison between psychophysical and electrophysiological findings.

claim: In human perception, rod → cone interactions were stronger than cone → rod interactions.
source: (1) rod → cone interactions were stronger than cone → rod interactions (Figure 1H)
evidence: This is a finding from the psychophysical experiments shown in Figure 1H.

claim: In human perception, rod → cone interactions were stronger for 0.2–0.3 s intervals between adapt and test flashes than for 1 s intervals.
source: (2) rod → cone interactions were stronger for 0.2–0.3 s intervals between adapt and test flashes than for 1 s intervals (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is a finding from the psychophysical experiments shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Retinal rod-cone interactions contribute substantially to perceptual interactions.
source: These similarities suggest that retinal rod-cone interactions contribute substantially to perceptual interactions
evidence: This is inferred from the similarities between retinal and perceptual measurements.

claim: Rod-mediated signals can traverse the retina through the dedicated rod bipolar circuitry.
source: Rod-mediated signals can traverse the retina through the dedicated rod bipolar circuitry and/or through cones via rod-cone gap junctions and then through the associated cone bipolar circuitry (DeVries and Baylor, 1995; Schneeweis and Schnapf, 1995) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about retinal circuitry, supported by citations.

claim: Rod-mediated signals can traverse the retina through cones via rod-cone gap junctions and then through the associated cone bipolar circuitry.
source: Rod-mediated signals can traverse the retina through the dedicated rod bipolar circuitry and/or through cones via rod-cone gap junctions and then through the associated cone bipolar circuitry (DeVries and Baylor, 1995; Schneeweis and Schnapf, 1995) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about retinal circuitry, supported by citations.

claim: The ratios of the amplitudes of the rod-mediated to cone-mediated responses were ~8 times smaller in L-cone synaptic terminals and horizontal cells than in ON RGCs.
source: The ratios of the amplitudes of the rod-mediated to cone-mediated responses were ∼8 times smaller in L-cone synaptic terminals and horizontal cells than in ON RGCs (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: At the light levels tested, rod-mediated signals appear to be routed through the dedicated rod bipolar circuitry until they reach the inner retina.
source: Thus, at these light levels rod-mediated signals appear to be routed through the dedicated rod bipolar circuitry until they reach the inner retina.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of rod/cone response ratios in different cell types.

claim: Independent pharmacological manipulation of the rod and cone bipolar circuits provided further support for the conclusion that rod signals are routed through the dedicated rod bipolar circuitry.
source: Independent pharmacological manipulation of the rod and cone bipolar circuits provided further support for this conclusion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In mouse retina, rod signals are transmitted in parallel through rod and cone bipolar circuits at the light levels tested.
source: This situation differs considerably from mouse retina, where rod signals are transmitted in parallel through rod and cone (via rod-cone gap junctions) bipolar circuits at these light levels (Grimes et al., 2014; Ke et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a comparison to findings in mouse retina, supported by citations.

claim: Horizontal cells receive direct synaptic input from cones.
source: horizontal cells receive direct synaptic input from cones and hence provide a direct measure of cone synaptic output (Trumpler et al., 2008) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about retinal circuitry, supported by a citation.

claim: Horizontal cells provide a direct measure of cone synaptic output.
source: horizontal cells receive direct synaptic input from cones and hence provide a direct measure of cone synaptic output (Trumpler et al., 2008) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical connectivity, supported by a citation.

claim: Horizontal cells, AII amacrine cells, and cone bipolar cells all combined rod- and cone-mediated responses linearly.
source: under conditions in which the RGC excitatory synaptic inputs exhibited strongly nonlinear responses, horizontal cells, AII amacrine cells, and cone bipolar cells all combined rod- and cone-mediated responses linearly—that is, the linear sum of the responses delivered individually matched the response to the flashes delivered sequentially (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The absence of nonlinear rod → cone interactions in circuit components upstream of the synapse between ON cone bipolar cells and RGCs, and presence of such interactions in the RGC excitatory synaptic inputs, indicates that such interactions must occur at the cone bipolar output synapse itself.
source: The absence of nonlinear rod → cone interactions in circuit components upstream of the synapse between ON cone bipolar cells and RGCs, and presence of such interactions in the RGC excitatory synaptic inputs (Figure 2F), indicates that such interactions must occur at the cone bipolar output synapse itself.
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of where nonlinear interactions are and are not observed in the circuit.

claim: The cone bipolar → RGC synapse could function as a gate keeper, controlling which types of photoreceptor signals are transmitted to an ON parasol RGC.
source: Because this synapse is shared by both the rod and cone bipolar circuits, it could function as a gate keeper, controlling which types of photoreceptor signals are transmitted to an ON parasol RGC.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings about where interactions occur.

claim: Vesicle depletion cannot easily account for the greater strength of rod → cone interactions compared to cone → rod interactions.
source: This mechanism, however, cannot easily account for the greater strength of rod → cone interactions compared to cone → rod interactions (Figure 1D,E) since similar synaptic activation, regardless of origin, would be expected to produce similar levels of vesicle depletion.
evidence: This is a logical argument against vesicle depletion as the mechanism, based on the asymmetry of the interactions.

claim: The kinetics of the rod- and cone-mediated voltage responses of ON cone bipolar cells differed substantially.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, the kinetics of the rod- and cone-mediated voltage responses of ON cone bipolar cells differed substantially (Figure 3A; similar differences were observed in AII amacrine responses)
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Rod-mediated responses in ON cone bipolar cells were biphasic, consisting of an initial depolarization followed by a slow hyperpolarization.
source: rod-mediated responses were biphasic, consisting of an initial depolarization (rightward blue arrow in Figure 3B) followed by a slow hyperpolarization (i.e., overshoot; leftward blue arrow in Figure 3B)
evidence: This is a description of the observed response kinetics shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The hyperpolarizing component of rod-mediated responses in ON cone bipolar cells depended on inhibition within the rod bipolar circuit.
source: the latter component depended on inhibition within the rod bipolar circuit (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cone-mediated responses in ON cone bipolar cells were faster and substantially less biphasic than rod-mediated responses.
source: Cone-mediated responses, in comparison, were faster and substantially less biphasic (red arrows in Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a description of the observed response kinetics shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Rod → cone suppression exhibited a time course consistent with that of the hyperpolarization in the rod-mediated ON cone bipolar voltage response.
source: Indeed, rod → cone suppression exhibited a time course consistent with that of the hyperpolarization in the rod-mediated ON cone bipolar voltage response (Figure 3A,C,D).
evidence: This is a comparison between the time course of suppression and the bipolar cell response kinetics, shown in Figure 3.

claim: Rod → cone suppression was maximal for time offsets between 0.1 and 0.3 s.
source: Across cells, rod → cone suppression was maximal for time offsets between 0.1 and 0.3 s, with little or no suppression for longer or shorter offsets (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Responses to simultaneously delivered rod and cone stimuli can be described by linear summation followed by saturation for strong stimuli.
source: The behavior at time offsets <0.1 s is consistent with previous work showing that responses to simultaneously delivered rod and cone stimuli can be described by linear summation followed by saturation for strong stimuli (Enroth-Cugell et al., 1977; Cao et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous findings, supported by citations.

claim: Linear filters for rod inputs were slower and more biphasic than those for cone inputs.
source: Linear filters for rod inputs were slower and more biphasic than those for cone inputs (Figure 4B), consistent with the differences observed in ON cone bipolar voltage responses (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the LN model analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The nonlinearities derived from rod and cone inputs were similar.
source: The nonlinearities derived from rod and cone inputs were similar (Figure 4C), consistent with a location in a shared element in the rod and cone circuits.
evidence: This is a finding from the LN model analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Across cells, the predicted and measured interaction indices were strongly correlated.
source: Across cells, the predicted and measured interaction indices were strongly correlated (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparison of model predictions to experimental data, shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The greater strength of rod → cone compared to cone → rod interactions in the LN model predictions depends directly on the rod linear filter being more biphasic than the cone filter.
source: The greater strength of rod → cone compared to cone → rod interactions in the LN model predictions depends directly on the rod linear filter being more biphasic than the cone filter
evidence: This is an explanation of the model mechanism that produces the asymmetry.

claim: A simple model based on linear summation of kinetically-distinct rod and cone responses followed by a rectifying nonlinearity can quantitatively predict the strength of interactions between rod- and cone-mediated flash responses.
source: Thus a simple model based on linear summation of kinetically-distinct rod and cone responses followed by a rectifying nonlinearity can quantitatively predict the strength of interactions between rod- and cone-mediated flash responses, including the asymmetry in relative interaction strength.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the model predictions matching experimental data.

claim: The rod bipolar circuit remains the dominant route through which rod-mediated signals traverse the retina at light levels well above cone threshold.
source: Surprisingly, we found that the rod bipolar circuit remains the dominant route through which rod-mediated signals traverse the retina at light levels well above cone threshold.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experiments comparing rod and cone response ratios in different cell types (Figure 2).

claim: Perceptual measures of rod-cone interactions and their dependence on light level are often interpreted in the context of the different routes that rod-mediated signals could take through the retina.
source: First, perceptual measures of rod-cone interactions and their dependence on light level are often interpreted in the context of the different routes that rod-mediated signals could take through the retina (reviewed in Buck, 2004, 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about how the field has interpreted perceptual data, supported by citations to reviews.

claim: The lack of mixing of rod- and cone-mediated signals constrains potential sites of interaction.
source: This lack of mixing of rod- and cone-mediated signals both constrains potential sites of interaction
evidence: This is a logical inference from the finding that signals remain segregated.

claim: The lack of mixing of rod- and cone-mediated signals provides opportunities for selective processing.
source: and provides ample opportunities for selective processing, for example to shape the kinetics of rod-mediated signals distinctly from cone-mediated signals.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the finding that signals remain segregated.

claim: Perceptual rod-cone interactions can be complex.
source: Second, perceptual rod-cone interactions can be complex—for example, the asymmetric nonlinear interactions we investigate here.
evidence: This is a general statement about the nature of the interactions studied.

claim: Apparently complex rod-cone interactions can be explained by a simple neural mechanism: linear summation of kinetically-distinct outputs from parallel circuits followed by a shared synaptic nonlinearity.
source: We show that these apparently complex interactions can be explained by a simple neural mechanism: linear summation of kinetically-distinct outputs from parallel circuits followed by a shared synaptic nonlinearity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling and experimental results.

claim: Non-human primate retina was obtained through the Tissue Distribution Program of the Regional Primate Research Center at the University of Washington.
source: Non-human primate retina was obtained through the Tissue Distribution Program of the Regional Primate Research Center at the University of Washington.
evidence: This is a statement about the source of experimental tissue.

claim: Extracellular recordings from ON parasol retinal ganglion cells used ~3 MΩ electrodes containing Ames medium.
source: Extracellular recordings from ON parasol retinal ganglion cells used ∼3 MΩ electrodes containing Ames medium.
evidence: This is a methodological detail.

claim: Cone terminals were identified by following axons from cone cell bodies to the margin of the outer plexiform layer.
source: Cone terminals were identified by following axons from cone cell bodies to the margin of the outer plexiform layer.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about cell identification.

claim: In initial experiments, cell types were confirmed by fluorescence imaging following recording.
source: In initial experiments, cell types were confirmed by fluorescence imaging following recording.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about cell identification.

claim: Visual perception experiments were conducted according the human subject guidelines laid forth by the University of Washington.
source: Visual perception experiments were conducted according the human subject guidelines laid forth by the University of Washington.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: Light intensities were converted to photoisomerization rates using the estimated collecting area of rods and cones, the stimulus emission spectra and the photoreceptor absorption spectra.
source: Light intensities (photons/μm2/s) were converted to photoisomerization rates (R*/photoreceptor/s) using the estimated collecting area of rods and cones (1 and 0.37 μm2, respectively), the stimulus (i.e., LED or monitor) emission spectra and the photoreceptor absorption spectra (Baylor et al., 1984, 1987).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about stimulus calibration, with citation support.

claim: The estimated collecting area of rods is 1 μm2.
source: using the estimated collecting area of rods and cones (1 and 0.37 μm2, respectively)
evidence: This is a parameter value used in the analysis, based on cited literature.

claim: The estimated collecting area of cones is 0.37 μm2.
source: using the estimated collecting area of rods and cones (1 and 0.37 μm2, respectively)
evidence: This is a parameter value used in the analysis, based on cited literature.

claim: Rod- and cone-preferring flashes were 10 ms in duration.
source: Rod- and cone- preferring flashes were 10 ms in duration.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the stimulus.

claim: For visual perception experiments, red and blue spots of ~2° were presented for 16 ms at ~10° eccentricity in human observers.
source: For visual perception experiments, red (peak power at 640 nm) and blue (peak power at 444 nm) spots of ∼2° were presented for 16 ms at ∼10° eccentricity in human observers.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the psychophysical stimulus.

claim: The filtered backlight of the monitor produced a mean luminance of ~1 R*/rod/s.
source: The filtered backlight of the monitor produced a mean luminance of ∼1 R*/rod/s.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the psychophysical stimulus.

claim: Both the predicted and measured interaction indices scaled with the degree of rectification in the nonlinearity as measured by the LN model.
source: Both the predicted and measured interaction indices scaled with the degree of rectification in the nonlinearity as measured by the LN model (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation, though the data is not shown.

claim: Predicted interactions peaked for time offsets near 200 ms, as observed experimentally.
source: Similarly, predicted interactions peaked for time offsets near 200 ms, as observed experimentally (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a comparison between model predictions and experimental observations shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Retinal interactions were inferred by comparing the perceptual matches obtained when adapt and test flashes were delivered to the same vs separate eyes.
source: Interactions arising from separate eye delivery must occur in higher brain regions with access to information from both eyes (e.g., cortical interactions) whereas interactions arising from same eye delivery would also include retinal interactions.
evidence: This is the logic of the psychophysical experimental design.

claim: Interactions arising from separate eye delivery must occur in higher brain regions with access to information from both eyes.
source: Interactions arising from separate eye delivery must occur in higher brain regions with access to information from both eyes (e.g., cortical interactions)
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the anatomy of the visual system.

claim: Retinal and cortical gain factors were assumed to be multiplicative and occur in series.
source: We assumed that retinal and cortical gain factors were multiplicative and occurred in series.
evidence: This is an assumption made in the analysis of the psychophysical data.

claim: Each observer conducted at least 1 training session before data was included for analysis.
source: Each observer conducted at least 1 training session before data was included for analysis.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the psychophysical experiments.

claim: Training sessions helped observers become comfortable with binocular fusion of images from distinct monitors.
source: These training sessions helped observers (1) become comfortable with binocular fusion of images from distinct monitors
evidence: This is a statement about the purpose of the training sessions.

claim: Training sessions helped observers improve their fixation while flashes are delivered to the peripheral retina.
source: (2) improve their fixation while flashes are delivered to the peripheral retina
evidence: This is a statement about the purpose of the training sessions.

claim: Training sessions helped observers become comfortable with the user interface.
source: (3) become comfortable with the user interface (e.g., entering responses, transitions between conditions).
evidence: This is a statement about the purpose of the training sessions.

claim: Rod-mediated responses in AII amacrine cells were monophonic in darkness and became biphasic as mean luminance was increased to 20 R*/rod/s.
source: Rod-mediated responses in AII amacrine cells were monophonic in darkness and became biphasic as mean luminance was increased to 20 R*/rod/s.
evidence: This is an observation from experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Inhibitory blockers significantly reduced the fast component of the overshoot in AII amacrine cell responses.
source: Inhibitory blockers significantly reduced the fast (∼200 ms after the flash) component of the overshoot, likely reflecting suppression of presynaptic inhibition to the rod bipolar cell terminal.
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The fast overshoot in AII amacrine cell responses recovered after returning to control solution for >8 min.
source: After returning to control solution for >8 min the fast overshoot recovered.
evidence: This is an observation from the pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Interaction indices for horizontal cells did not differ significantly from 0.
source: Interaction indices for horizontal cells (p = 0.49), AIIs (p = 0.45) and cone bipolars (p = 0.49) did not differ significantly from 0, while those of RGCs did (p < 10−7).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Interaction indices for AII amacrine cells did not differ significantly from 0.
source: Interaction indices for horizontal cells (p = 0.49), AIIs (p = 0.45) and cone bipolars (p = 0.49) did not differ significantly from 0, while those of RGCs did (p < 10−7).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Interaction indices for cone bipolar cells did not differ significantly from 0.
source: Interaction indices for horizontal cells (p = 0.49), AIIs (p = 0.45) and cone bipolars (p = 0.49) did not differ significantly from 0, while those of RGCs did (p < 10−7).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Interaction indices for retinal ganglion cells differed significantly from 0.
source: Interaction indices for horizontal cells (p = 0.49), AIIs (p = 0.45) and cone bipolars (p = 0.49) did not differ significantly from 0, while those of RGCs did (p < 10−7).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claim: NBQX is an AMPAR antagonist.
source: NBQX, an AMPAR antagonist
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge.

claim: Bath application of NBQX selectively eliminated input from the rod bipolar pathway to AII amacrine cells.
source: Bath application of NBQX selectively eliminated input from the rod bipolar pathway.
evidence: This is a finding from the pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The greater sensitivity of the rod-mediated response to NBQX indicates that most of this response is conveyed through the rod bipolar cell.
source: Instead, the greater sensitivity of the rod-mediated response to NBQX indicates that most of this response is conveyed through the rod bipolar cell.
evidence: This is inferred from the pharmacological results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Similar results were obtained in AII amacrine cells regardless of recording configuration (voltage-clamp vs current-clamp).
source: Similar results were obtained regardless of recording configuration.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.
